blocks.text: 109 מוּסָף לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 109
uncertainties: The running head is cut off at the top of band 1. The vowels on מוסף and לְיוֹם were read from the full-page image at low resolution.

blocks.text: יְסוֹדוֹ מֵעָפָר וְסוֹפוֹ לֶעָפָר. בְּנַפְשׁוֹ יָבִיא לַחְמוֹ. מָשׁוּל כַּחֶרֶס הַנִּשְׁבָּר. כְּחָצִיר יָבֵשׁ. וּכְצִיץ נוֹבֵל. כְּצֵל עוֹבֵר. וְכֶעָנָן כָּלֶה. וּכְרוּחַ נוֹשָׁבֶת. וּכְאָבָק פּוֹרֵחַ. וְכַחֲלוֹם יָעוּף:
uncertainties: This paragraph continues the Unetaneh Tokef from the previous page (earlier-work material).
There may be a small accent or meteg on כַּחֶרֶס; it was not recorded.

blocks.text: וְאַתָּה הוּא מֶלֶךְ אֵל חַי וְקַיָּם:
uncertainties: This line is set in very large display type, and the lamed of אֵל is an oversized glyph. The vowel points under the large letters (including the final-kaf sheva and the dagesh in וְקַיָּם) were read from the display face.

blocks.text: ח׳
uncertainties: The small role abbreviation could be ח׳ (chazzan) or ק׳ (congregation). It reads most like ח׳.

blocks.text: אֵין קִצְבָּה לִשְׁנוֹתֶיךָ. וְאֵין קֵצָה (נ״א קֵץ) לְאֹרֶךְ יָמֶיךָ. וְאֵין לְשַׁעֵר מַרְכְּבוֹת כְּבוֹדֶךָ. וְאֵין לְפָרֵשׁ עֵילוּם שְׁמֶךָ. שִׁמְךָ נָאֶה לְךָ וְאַתָּה נָאֶה לִשְׁמֶךָ. וּשְׁמֵנוּ קָרָאתָ בִּשְׁמֶךָ:
uncertainties: The parenthetical (נ״א קֵץ) is a source variant printed in small type inside the line. It is kept in place.
The vowel under the ayin of עֵילוּם appears to be tsere. Whether the vav has a shuruk dot or is a holam is unclear.

blocks.text: קו״ח
uncertainties: This small abbreviation is unclear: the middle letter could be ו or ר (קר״ח). It is most likely קו״ח, meaning congregation and chazzan.

blocks.text: עֲשֵׂה לְמַעַן שְׁמֶךָ. וְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת שִׁמְךָ עַל מַקְדִּישֵׁי שְׁמֶךָ:
חזן
כְּסוֹד שִׂיחַ שַׂרְפֵי קֹדֶשׁ. הַמַּקְדִּישִׁים שִׁמְךָ בַּקֹּדֶשׁ. דָּרֵי מַעְלָה עִם דָּרֵי מַטָּה קוֹרְאִים וּמְשַׁלְּשִׁים בִּשְׁלוּשׁ קְדֻשָּׁה בַּקֹּדֶשׁ.
uncertainties: This passage is set in larger type with widely stretched word spacing on the last line. The extra spacing is layout only.
There may be a meteg or accent on דָּרֵי and מַעְלָה; it was not recorded.

blocks.text: ח׳
כַּכָּתוּב עַל יַד נְבִיאֶךָ. וְקָרָא זֶה אֶל זֶה וְאָמַר.
קו״ח
uncertainties: This is the same unclear abbreviation as at עֲשֵׂה (it could also be קר״ח).

blocks.text: קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ יְיָ צְבָאוֹת מְלֹא כָל־הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ:
uncertainties: The divine name is printed as יְיָ. There may be an accent on הָאָרֶץ; it was not recorded.

blocks.text: ק׳
כְּבוֹדוֹ מָלֵא עוֹלָם מְשָׁרְתָיו שׁוֹאֲלִים זֶה לָזֶה אַיֵּה מְקוֹם כְּבוֹדוֹ לְעֻמָּתָם בָּרוּךְ יֹאמֵרוּ:
uncertainties: This text ends with בָּרוּךְ יֹאמֵרוּ. The page does not print Ezekiel 3:12 (בָּרוּךְ כְּבוֹד יְיָ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ), so it may be an implied cue that needs expanding. It was not added.

blocks.text: ע״ס א״ב ובסוף חתום שם המחבר אלעזר.
uncertainties: This is printed in very small unpointed type. The first token could be עי״ס or ע״ס. ובסוף could also be read וכסוף, since ב and כ are hard to tell apart at this size; ובסוף is the more likely reading.

blocks.text: ק׳

וְחַיּוֹת אֲשֶׁר הֵנָּה מְרֻבָּעוֹת כִּסֵּא. בְּמָאתַיִם וַחֲמִשִּׁים וָשֵׁשׁ מַכְנִיפוֹת כִּסֵּא. גּוֹעֲשׁוֹת בּוֹ בְּסוֹכְכָם פָּנִים בְּפָנִים לַכִּסֵּא. דְּמוּת רָקִיעַ בְּרֹאשָׁם נָטוּי לַכִּסֵּא. הוּא כְּעֵין הַקֶּרַח בּוֹ שְׁבִיב כִּסֵּא. וּמִמַּעַל לָרָקִיעַ כְּמַרְאֵה דְּמוּת כִּסֵּא. זָעוֹת בְּלִי לֵאוּת מֵהִיל כִּסֵּא.
uncertainties: בְּרֹאשָׁם may be printed בְּרָאשָׁם; the vowel above or below the resh is unclear.
The vowel under the mem of מֵהִיל looks like tsere.

blocks.text: ח׳
uncertainties: This abbreviation is printed in the middle of the line, before חָשׁוֹת.

blocks.text: חָשׁוֹת בְּרָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב מֵרְעִישׁוֹת (נ״א מַרְעִישׁוֹת) כִּסֵּא. טָסוֹת כַּבָּזָק וְלֹא מְזִיזוֹת הוֹד כִּסֵּא. יוֹדְעוֹת כִּי כָל מָקוֹם לֹא יָכִיל מְקוֹם כִּסֵּא:
uncertainties: The vowels in the main reading מֵרְעִישׁוֹת are unclear: the mark under the mem looks like tsere, with sheva under the resh. The variant in parentheses reads מַרְעִישׁוֹת.
כַּבָּזָק: the first kaf appears to have patach and the bet a dagesh. It could be כְּבָזָק.

blocks.text: 109 Musaph for the New Year 109

his end is dust, at the risk of his life he earns his bread, he is to be compared to a broken potsherd, to dry grass, to a withering flower, to a passing shadow, to a drifting cloud, to a gust of wind, to blown dust and to a fleeting dream.
uncertainties: This continues from the previous page (earlier-work material).

blocks.text: But Thou art King, O God, living and enduring
uncertainties: Printed in italics.

blocks.text: אין

There is no limit to Thy years and no end to the length of Thy days, one cannot measure the chariots of Thy glory nor fathom the mystery of Thy Name; Thy Name is fitting for Thee and Thou art fitting for Thy Name and our name hast Thou called by Thy Name. Act for Thy Name's sake and sanctify Thy Name upon those who sanctify Thy Name.
כסוד

According to the mystic utterance of the holy Seraphim, who sanctify Thy Name in holiness, those who dwell above and those who dwell below, proclaim three times the threefold sanctification in sanctity, as it is written through Thy prophet, once calls to the other and says:
uncertainties: Seraphim is hyphenated across a line break as Ser-/aphim and has been rejoined here.

blocks.text: קדוש
‘Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is full of His glory’.
כבודו
His glory fills the world, His servants ask one of the other: ‘Where is the site of His glory?’ Those opposite them say: ‘Blessed . . .’.
uncertainties: The page ends here. The piyyut וְחַיּוֹת (from the Hebrew page) is not translated on this page.

notes: On s238, the upper part (from יְסוֹדוֹ through the large heading line וְאַתָּה הוּא מֶלֶךְ) is the end of the Unetaneh Tokef, which is earlier-work material. It is included because the instructions ask for complete pages.
There are no footnotes on either page. The only small-type notes are the two source variants marked נ״א (kept in place in the text) and the rubric about the alphabetical acrostic signed אלעזר.
Role abbreviations are given as separate speaker blocks. The abbreviation printed at עֲשֵׂה and קָדוֹשׁ is uncertain (קו״ח or קר״ח).
כְּבוֹדוֹ ends with בָּרוּךְ יֹאמֵרוּ, and the English ends with ‘Blessed . . .’. Both are implied cues for Ezekiel 3:12, which the page does not print. Nothing was added.
The Hebrew page was read from the full scan and all four enlarged bands. The English page was read from the full scan only, which was clearly legible; its enlarged bands were not opened.
The English page does not translate the piyyut וְחַיּוֹת, the acrostic rubric, or the Hebrew speaker labels.
